draft.title: Literature from different contexts
card: Stories, poems and plays come from many times and places. Some were written long ago and some were written this year.
the time, place and culture a text comes from. It shapes what a text shows, such as the setting, the problems characters face and the values they hold.
First Nations Australian authors write stories, poems and plays too. Their works often draw on their own Country, communities and cultures.
Knowing the context helps a reader understand why characters act as they do. It also shows how life can differ from one time or place to another.
draft.remember: A text's context shapes what it shows, so reading widely lets you see other times, places and cultures.

a.q: What does the context of a text mean?
opts: The time, place and culture the text comes from
The order in which the events of the story happen
The feelings the reader has while reading the text
The person who tells the story to the reader
a.why: Context is the time, place and culture a text comes from. The order of events is the plot, and the person who tells the story is the narrator, which is a different idea from context.
a.clue: Think about when, where and among whom a text was made.

b.q: Sam reads a play written long ago in a faraway country. The characters hold beliefs that seem unusual to Sam. What best explains this?
opts: The play shows the values of its own time and place
The author wanted to confuse readers on purpose
The play must be about a different topic from today
The characters were written without any beliefs
b.why: A text's context shapes what it shows, including the values of its characters. The beliefs seem unusual to Sam because they come from another time and place. The other options claim things the card does not support.
b.clue: Ask where and when the play was written.

a.best: The time, place and culture the text comes from

b.best: The play shows the values of its own time and place

Knowing the context helps a reader understand why characters act as they do. It also shows how life can differ from one time or place to another.
proposal.remember: A text's context shapes what it shows, so reading widely lets you see other times, places and cultures.

a.q: What does the context of a text mean?
opts: The time, place and culture the text comes from
The order in which the events of the story happen
The feelings the reader has while reading the text
The person who tells the story to the reader
a.why: Context is the time, place and culture a text comes from. The order of events and the person telling the story are parts of the story itself. They do not tell you where or when the text was made.
a.clue: Think about when, where and among whom a text was made.

b.q: Sam reads a play written long ago in a faraway country. The characters hold beliefs that seem unusual to Sam. What best explains this?
opts: The play shows the values of its own time and place
The author wanted to confuse readers on purpose
The play must be about a different topic from today
The characters were written without any beliefs
b.why: A text's context shapes what it shows, including the values its characters hold. The beliefs seem unusual because they come from another time and place. Different beliefs do not mean the play's topic is different, since people in any time can face similar problems.
b.clue: Ask where and when the play was written.
